topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture and outlines the key learning outcomes regarding cellular transformation and cancer genetics.

topics.label: Tumor viruses, proto-oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the discovery that cancer-causing viruses transduce cellular proto-oncogenes and describe the laboratory assays used to test cellular transformation.

topics.label: Functional classes, pathways, and allele dynamics of cancer genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional definitions of oncogenes and tumor suppressors, illustrating their regulatory mechanisms in the cell cycle and the effects of allele dosage and dominant negative mutations.

topics.label: Mechanisms, repair pathways, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how defects in DNA repair, replication proofreading, and mitotic chromosome segregation produce sequence and chromosomal instability and induce cellular stress.

topics.label: Multistep progression and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how sequential somatic mutations and inherited germline defects drive multi-step tumor development and clinical cancer syndromes.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture, offers to answer questions, and recommends further reading.
